opportunity: A load that reads bytes a later store overwrites could print after that store: one base plus two different constant offsets counted as two objects whatever the access widths, so `mov eax,[rdi+7]; mov [rdi+8],sil` printed `*(char *)(a0 + 8) = a1; return *(unsigned int *)(a0 + 7);`, which returns the new byte

change_kind: strict correctness fix (no option: it only stops a load from printing after a store that overwrites some of its bytes)
inspiration: Ghidra ActionMarkImplied::isPossibleAlias / isPossibleAliasStep (coreaction.cc); upstream master f9e13846 has the same hole and a FIXME on its constant arm
root_cause: ActionMarkImplied::checkImpliedCover forces a LOAD explicit when its cover crosses a STORE whose pointer isPossibleAlias says may equal the load's. isPossibleAlias compares pointer VALUES only: a pointer plus any constant (isPossibleAliasStep), one base plus two different constants (INT_ADD arm: !functionalEquality(bases)), and two different constant addresses all answer 'different', whatever the access widths, so a 4-byte load at base+7 was judged independent of a 1-byte store at base+8.
fix: p6_variables/coreaction_cleanup.rs: check_implied_cover passes the store's value size and the load's output size (AliasSpan {w1, w2, scale}); a constant step, two distinct constants off functionally equal bases, or two constant addresses answer 'different' only when [o1,o1+w1) and [o2,o2+w2) are disjoint (distance taken signed at the pointer size). A distance between two PTRADD indices is scaled by the element size; a negation reverses it; an XOR by a constant is at least its lowest set bit away in either direction. Commuted matches are only taken for byte-scaled adds. The predicate answers 'may alias' everywhere main's did, so the fix can only turn implied loads explicit.
